aggravating_circumstances: Callous and brutal murder of wife, possession of blood-stained weapon
mitigating_circumstances: No hurt or discomfort to child, conduct before and after incident suggests mental capacity
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Upheld trial court's conviction and sentence
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, assaulted his wife with a chopper on her neck in their bedroom, resulting in her death. The victim's body was discovered by neighbors, covered in blood. The accused was seen by witnesses carrying a blood-stained chopper and his 8-month-old son. The medical examination of the victim's body confirmed injuries consistent with the weapon seized from the accused. The accused claimed insanity due to paranoid schizophrenia, but the courts found no evidence he was mentally ill at the time of the crime. The accused had a history of treatment for a psychotic disorder in 1985, but there was no indication of mental illness post-1985. The accused's actions, including leaving the child with a neighbor and confessing to the crime, suggested he understood the nature of his actions.
